_about: Curated from official programme websites. Each record lists the official page, when it was last checked, and honest deadline notes (many programmes publish dates only shortly before opening). Edit this file and restart the app (or run npm run import) to update the catalogue.

scholarships.title: UNHCR DAFI Tertiary Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: DAFI funds university-level study for qualified refugees (and returnees in some countries) in their country of asylum. It mainly covers bachelor's programmes and some short-cycle or accredited TVET courses; it does not fund master's degrees. Each country office runs its own call.
scholarships.eligibility: Rwanda 2026-27 call: recognised refugee or asylum seeker in Rwanda, already admitted to a Rwandan university, strong academic results. One applicant per family. Not open to people already holding another higher-education scholarship or confirmed for third-country resettlement. Criteria differ by country; check your UNHCR country office.
scholarships.award_value: Package varies by country: tuition, materials, food, transport, accommodation
scholarships.deadline_note: Calls are country-specific and yearly. The Rwanda 2026-27 call ran 15 Jul to 7 Aug 2026 and is closed; the next call date is not published. Watch your UNHCR country help page (help.unhcr.org).
scholarships.how_to_apply: Watch your country's UNHCR help site for the yearly DAFI call. Fill in the online DAFI application form and upload your UNHCR registration proof, high school diploma, university admission letter and equivalence certificate. Digital Career Counsellors or Community Centres can help with connectivity problems.

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Makerere University (Undergraduate)
scholarships.description: A full scholarship for academically talented young Africans who cannot afford university, studying at Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda. 245 undergraduate scholarships were offered for 2026/27, with places reserved for refugees and displaced youth, young people with disabilities, international students and refugee-hosting communities.
scholarships.eligibility: First-year entrant admitted (or applying for admission) to Makerere main campus under the private sponsorship scheme. Completed advanced secondary school in an African country, or holds a diploma with at least a second-class/credit award (refugees may instead pass Makerere's mature-age entry exam). Financial need and proof of leadership or community service. Age 28 or under at the deadline (up to 32 for refugees, IDPs and people with disabilities). Must not hold another scholarship. Refugees need a valid Refugee ID card or Family Attestation.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship (the page does not itemise what it covers)
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/27 call closed on 5 June 2026. The next call date is not published yet. Watch the Makerere application portal each year.
scholarships.how_to_apply: 1) Apply for admission to Makerere main campus (private sponsorship scheme). 2) Fill in the free online scholarship form on the Makerere Mastercard Foundation portal, using a computer. 3) Submit before the deadline; incomplete forms are disqualified. Only shortlisted applicants are contacted. The process is free: anyone asking for money is a fraudster (info@mastercardfdn.mak.ac.ug).

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Makerere University (Master's)
scholarships.description: Scholarships for young Africans to do a master's degree at Makerere University in Kampala. 13 master's scholarships were offered for 2026/27: at least 70% for young women, at least 25% for refugees and IDPs and at least 10% for people with disabilities.
scholarships.eligibility: Applied for admission to Makerere main campus. Undergraduate degree completed in an African country. Financial need, leadership or community service. Age 35 or under at the deadline (40 for refugees, IDPs and people with disabilities). Must not hold another scholarship or already be doing or have finished a master's. Must apply for one of the priority programmes listed on the call page.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship (the page does not itemise what it covers)
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/27 call closed on 5 June 2026. The next call date is not published yet. Watch the Makerere application portal each year.
scholarships.how_to_apply: 1) Apply for admission to Makerere main campus. 2) Fill in the free online scholarship form on the Makerere Mastercard Foundation portal. Only shortlisted applicants are contacted; if you hear nothing by the end of August, it was unsuccessful. Never pay anyone for a place.

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda (Undergraduate)
scholarships.description: Full scholarships for talented young people from economically disadvantaged backgrounds to study an undergraduate degree at the University of Rwanda. Refugees have been a named priority group in past calls (UNHCR Rwanda announced it).
scholarships.eligibility: Admission application to the University of Rwanda (you need a UR reference number), academic strength, economic disadvantage, leadership and community engagement. In the 2025 call for refugees: age 30 or under. Criteria can change each year; read the current call.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship (the page does not itemise what it covers)
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/27 undergraduate call (Cohort 5) ran until 12 October 2026 and is closed. The next call date is not published yet.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply to the University of Rwanda for admission first and get your UR reference number, then complete the Scholars Program application on the University of Rwanda recruitment portal and upload your documents as small PDFs. Questions: mcfsp@ur.ac.rw (include your full name and application number).

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Rwanda (Postgraduate)
scholarships.description: Full scholarships for talented young people from economically disadvantaged backgrounds to study a postgraduate degree at the University of Rwanda.
scholarships.eligibility: See the current call on the University of Rwanda recruitment portal: the page lists the track as full scholarships for talented young people from economically disadvantaged backgrounds. Check age, degree and admission requirements there.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship (the page does not itemise what it covers)
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/27 postgraduate call ran from 23 July to 25 August 2026 and is closed. The next call date is not published yet.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Log in or register on the University of Rwanda recruitment portal and complete the postgraduate Scholars Program application when the call opens. Questions: mcfsp@ur.ac.rw.

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at African Leadership University (ALU)
scholarships.description: A full scholarship programme for undergraduate study at ALU in Kigali, Rwanda, for promising young leaders from across Africa. The Foundation stresses young women, refugees and young people with disabilities.
scholarships.eligibility: The Foundation page lists no detailed criteria. Read the requirements on the ALU programme page before you apply.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship (the page does not itemise what it covers)
scholarships.deadline_note: No dates are published on the Foundation page (it says admissions are open). Check the ALU programme page for the current intake and deadline.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Open the ALU programme page and follow its application steps. Apply early and read the eligibility and documents list there.

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at EARTH University (Costa Rica)
scholarships.description: Full scholarships for young leaders from disadvantaged communities to study a four-year undergraduate degree in agricultural sciences and sustainability at EARTH University, near Limon in Costa Rica. About one third of scholars come from Sub-Saharan Africa and the rest from Latin America and the Caribbean. The programme has run since 2011 and also provides mentoring, career counselling, service-learning and internships. About 120 students are admitted each year.
scholarships.eligibility: Completed (or finishing) secondary school: you upload grades from your last three secondary years and your diploma in one PDF (max 4 MB). Three references who are not family members, and a video introduction of up to two minutes. Candidates are preferably between 17 and 30 years old. Admission weighs grades, references, tests, interviews and a socioeconomic study; financial aid is decided after you are admitted. Refugees and displaced people and young people with disabilities are named priority groups.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship (tuition, housing, food, medical insurance). EARTH lists the full cost at about US$36,856 a year for non-scholarship students.
scholarships.deadline_note: The admissions page lists applications for the next intake from 1 September to 15 November 2026. Its FAQ says forms close in January each year, so confirm the exact date with admisiones@earth.ac.cr.
scholarships.how_to_apply: 1) Create an account on the EARTH admissions site (admissions.earth.ac.cr). 2) Log in at apply.earth.ac.cr, fill in your details, answer the questions and upload your documents. 3) If shortlisted: aptitude and psychometric tests, then interviews (about March), then admission and immigration help (about May). Arrival is in mid-August. Questions: admisiones@earth.ac.cr.

scholarships.title: HELB Higher Education Loans and Bursaries
scholarships.description: Kenya's government student financing body, which gives loans, bursaries and scholarships to students at public and private universities and TVET colleges. Funding follows a graduated, needs-assessed model. Postgraduate scholarships are also offered.
scholarships.eligibility: Kenyan students with an admission letter from a university or TVET institution. First-time applicants register on the portal; continuing students use *642#, the HELB app or M-PESA mini app. Undergraduate loans apply to bachelor's students in East African Community universities; interest is 4%.
scholarships.award_value: Loans, bursaries and scholarships; amount set by assessed need
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/27 first-time portal exists but the page states no closing date and its timer shows 'Closed'. Check the HELB portal or contact centre for the current window.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Get your admission letter, then register and apply on the HELB student portal (portal.hef.co.ke) with your ID or KCSE index number. Have parent and two guarantor details, photo and bank or M-PESA details ready. Continuing students apply via *642# or the HELB app.

scholarships.title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
scholarships.description: A competitive postgraduate award for outstanding students with no other way to fund their studies. Master's study is prioritised and PhDs are considered. Awards are half grant and half loan, and applications go through local AKF contacts.
scholarships.eligibility: Applicants must be in a listed country (including Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda; Rwanda, Burundi, DR Congo, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Somalia are not listed). Strong academics, a bachelor's degree, genuine financial need and admission to a reputable postgraduate institution. Preference under 30. Not for study in the UK or Russia.
scholarships.award_value: 50% grant, 50% loan: tuition and living costs; not travel
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026-2027 cycle is closed. The page says the next cycle opens in early 2027; no date published.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Use the eligibility tool on the AKDN site to find your local AKF contact in a listed country, then apply through them when the cycle opens. Plan multiple funding sources, since the programme is a last resort.

scholarships.title: Pan African University Scholarships
scholarships.provider: African Union Commission, Pan African University
scholarships.description: Fully funded postgraduate study at Pan African University institutes, run by the African Union. Covers MSc, MA and a PhD programme in fields such as water, energy, climate, governance and health sciences. Open to African nationals and the diaspora.
scholarships.eligibility: Young qualified applicants from African countries and the Diaspora. Master's: no older than 25 (men) or 28 (women), with a second-class upper degree or equivalent. PhD: no older than 28 (men) or 30 (women), with a relevant master's. Shortlisted candidates may sit exams.
scholarships.award_value: Full scholarship from the African Union Commission
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/27 call closed 15 December 2025. The 2027/28 call is not yet published; calls have opened around November in past years.
scholarships.how_to_apply: When the call opens, apply online through the PAU submission portal with certified transcripts, ID, CV, recommendation letters (and a concept note for PhD). Late applications are not considered.

scholarships.title: Rotary Peace Fellowships
scholarships.description: Fellowships for emerging peace and development leaders to study at a Rotary Peace Center. Master's degree and professional development certificate options exist. Selected fellows are notified in November.
scholarships.eligibility: Not for doctoral study. Applicants must not be active Rotary members or Rotary staff, and need at least three years between their last degree and start date. Must not currently be enrolled in a degree programme. English proficiency required. Certificate at Makerere (Uganda) needs an Africa connection. No nationality limit seen on pages read.
scholarships.award_value: Not stated on the pages read; see Rotary's fellowship page
scholarships.deadline_note: Annual: the page read says submissions run February to 15 May for the following academic year. The next exact date is not published on the pages read.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply online on My Rotary in the February to May window with a resume, recommendations, essays, a video statement and English test scores (transcripts for master's). Then apply separately for university admission.

scholarships.title: Chevening Scholarships
scholarships.description: Fully funded one-year master's scholarships in the UK for emerging leaders. Applicants apply through the Chevening country page for their citizenship, and must plan to return home for at least two years afterwards.
scholarships.eligibility: Citizen of a Chevening-eligible country (Rwanda, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Burundi, DR Congo, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Somalia all appear in the official country selector; check your own country page). At least two years (2,800 hours) of work experience after your first degree, a degree qualifying for a UK master's, and a commitment to return home for two years.
scholarships.award_value: Described as fully funded; itemised cover not read
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2027/28 round opened in August 2026 and closed in October 2026 (the exact day is on each country page). Check the official page for the next round.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Choose your country on the Chevening Apply page, pick Scholarship, and apply online through that country's page during the annual window.

scholarships.title: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
scholarships.provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC)
scholarships.description: Funded one-year master's study in the UK for people from lower and middle income Commonwealth countries. The CSC takes no direct applications: candidates apply to a national nominating agency or selected NGO, then through the CSC online system.
scholarships.eligibility: You must apply through your national nominating agency (or a selected nominating charity), not directly to the CSC. Among East African countries, citizens of Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda are eligible.
scholarships.award_value: Tuition, airfare, stipend GBP 1,712/month (GBP 2,000 London)
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2027/28 round closed on 20 October 2026. Nominators must submit nominations by December 2026. Check the official page for the next round.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply to your country's nominating body (it may set its own deadline) and also submit through the CSC Central online system with transcripts, ID and two references.

scholarships.title: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
scholarships.description: Scholarships for graduates from development and newly industrialised countries to study selected development-related master's courses in Germany. You apply directly to the course, not to DAAD.
scholarships.eligibility: Graduate from an eligible developing country (listed on the DAAD page via a DAC country list; check your country), top-third first degree usually no more than six years old, at least two years of related work after the degree, and no more than 15 months' residence in Germany at the deadline. Language requirements depend on the course.
scholarships.award_value: EUR 992/month plus insurance and travel allowance
scholarships.deadline_note: Deadlines are set per course; DAAD publishes a course-by-course deadline list (the 2026/27 list had dates between about Aug 2025 and mid-2026). Check each course for the 2027/2028 intake.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply directly to up to three EPOS courses with the EPOS form, CV, motivation letter, employer recommendation, work certificates and transcripts. DAAD does not forward applications.

scholarships.title: Fulbright Foreign Student Program
scholarships.provider: U.S. Department of State / Institute of International Education (Fulbright)
scholarships.description: Fulbright funds graduate study, young professionals and artists from abroad to study in the US. Applications run country by country through the local Fulbright Commission or US Embassy.
scholarships.eligibility: Varies by country and award. The official site says that if your country is not in its dropdown you cannot apply. Its list includes Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan and DR Congo (Kinshasa); Ethiopia, Burundi and Somalia did not appear.
scholarships.award_value: Varies by country; not stated on the page
scholarships.deadline_note: Deadlines are set by country and award; the page gives none. Confirm with your local Fulbright office.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Select your country on the Foreign Fulbright site and apply through the Fulbright Commission or US Embassy in your home country, which runs selection.

scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
scholarships.provider: European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA), European Union
scholarships.description: Joint master's degrees run by consortia of European universities, some of which offer scholarships to outstanding students from any country. Each master has its own application process and deadline.
scholarships.eligibility: Master's-level students from any country may apply. Scholarship availability and criteria differ for each programme, and some programmes no longer have scholarships.
scholarships.award_value: Not stated on the catalogue page
scholarships.deadline_note: Set by each master; most ask for applications between October and January for the following academic year.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Browse the official catalogue, choose a master, and apply on that programme's own website, checking there for scholarship availability.

scholarships.title: Australia Awards Africa
scholarships.description: Awards for suitably qualified Africans from eligible countries to study postgraduate courses in Australia or short courses, aimed at emerging leaders. Applications run in annual intakes.
scholarships.eligibility: The pre-screening form lists DR Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda among 25 African countries (Burundi, South Sudan and Somalia did not appear). Form asks for age 25+ by 1 Feb 2028, at least 5 years of related post-graduate work experience, an undergraduate degree, and no previous long-term Australia Award.
scholarships.award_value: Not stated on page checked
scholarships.deadline_note: 2027 intake closed. The 2028 intake is expected to open in February 2027; no exact date or deadline published.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Check eligibility via the pre-screening form on the site, then apply when the 2028 intake opens; dates will be announced on the Apply page.

scholarships.title: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
scholarships.provider: Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and participating Dutch institutions (Nuffic / Study in NL)
scholarships.description: A EUR 5,000 first-year scholarship for non-EEA students starting a full-time bachelor's or master's at a participating Dutch university. It is partial funding, not full tuition, and each institution runs its own selection.
scholarships.eligibility: Non-EEA nationality (so open to East African students), full-time bachelor's or master's at a participating Dutch institution, meeting that institution's entry requirements, and no previous degree from a Dutch institution. Each institution sets eligible fields.
scholarships.award_value: EUR 5,000 paid in first year
scholarships.deadline_note: Deadlines are set by each participating institution; the page gives no dates.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Find a participating institution on the Study in NL page and apply through that institution by its own deadline.

scholarships.title: Turkiye Burslari (Turkish Government Scholarships)
scholarships.provider: Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities, Republic of Turkiye
scholarships.description: A merit-based Turkish government scholarship for international students at associate, bachelor's, master's and PhD level, plus a research track. Awardees are placed in a Turkish university and department and get a living stipend and other support.
scholarships.eligibility: Described as competitive and merit-based, open to international applicants at associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and research level. The pages read did not state age limits, grade requirements or which nationalities are eligible; see the Criteria & Scholarship Programs page and FAQ before applying.
scholarships.award_value: Tuition, stipend, housing, health insurance, Turkish course, one flight ticket
scholarships.deadline_note: Official calendar shows the general application period as 10 January to 20 February each year (results early August). The 2027 dates have not been posted yet; the 2026 round is closed.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply free of charge through the online application system (tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr) during the application window; the site has an Application in 5 Steps guide.

scholarships.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) - Undergraduate Degree
scholarships.provider: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Government of the Republic of Korea
scholarships.description: Korean government scholarship for international students to do a Korean-language year followed by an associate or bachelor's degree at a designated Korean university. A separate GKS graduate programme exists and is not covered here.
scholarships.eligibility: Applicant and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship. Under 25 in the application year. High school (or associate degree) graduate or expected graduate, with cumulative score of 80% or higher, top 20% of the class, or the required CGPA. Embassy Track applicants must be from a country covered by Korean embassy recruitment; check with the Korean embassy.
scholarships.award_value: Airfare, language training, tuition and monthly allowance
scholarships.deadline_note: Official schedule: announcement in September; Embassy Track submissions in September; University Track submissions September to November; results in December. The 2027 undergraduate notices were posted on 9 and 23 Sept 2026, but exact deadline dates were not readable; check the notices.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Embassy Track: apply online through Study in Korea following your Korean embassy's guidelines. University Track: apply directly to a GKS university. Details are in the GKS notices; questions go to gksniied@korea.kr.

scholarships.title: MEXT Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho) Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan
scholarships.description: Fully funded Japanese government scholarship for study at Japanese universities. Embassy Recommendation categories include undergraduate, specialized training college and research (master's/PhD) students. Applicants apply through the Japanese embassy in their own country.
scholarships.eligibility: Example from the Tanzania embassy for the 2027 round: undergraduate applicants born on or after 2 April 2002 (under 25) with 12 years of schooling; research students under 35 with a bachelor's degree and GPA of at least 3.5/5. Undergraduate fields are natural or social sciences. Rules vary by country; check your embassy.
scholarships.award_value: Fully funded: tuition, living expenses, travel (per embassy pages)
scholarships.deadline_note: Recruitment for students arriving the following April happens in April-May of the previous year, with embassy screening May-August; schedule varies by country. The 2027 round closed in May 2026 (Tanzania 21 May, Ethiopia 29 May). The 2028 round dates are not published yet.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Read the Application Guidelines, then submit the application form, health certificate and recommendation letter to the Japanese embassy in your country. Do not send documents to MEXT in Japan; Tanzania and Ethiopia accept postal or hand delivery only.

scholarships.title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)
scholarships.provider: China Scholarship Council (CSC), Government of China
scholarships.description: Fully funded Chinese government scholarship for international students at undergraduate, master's and doctoral level, plus general and senior scholar categories. Applicants usually apply through the Chinese embassy in their country and on the CSC online system.
scholarships.eligibility: Citizen of the applying country and in good health. Undergraduate: high school graduate under 25; master's under 35; doctoral under 40. Must meet the target university's admission and language requirements (HSK 3 or 4 for Chinese-taught programmes). Bachelor's applicants need a CSCA score report. Rules and nomination channels vary by country; check your Chinese embassy.
scholarships.award_value: Tuition waiver, free housing, stipend, medical insurance; own airfare
scholarships.deadline_note: Windows are set by each Chinese embassy. The 2026/2027 round ran about Nov 2025 to Feb 2026 (e.g. Fiji embassy 1 Feb 2026). The 2027/2028 East African dates have not been published or found.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Register at campuschina.org, choose the Type A category and your embassy's agency number, pick up to three universities and upload documents including pre-admission papers. Then complete your embassy's own submission steps.

scholarships.title: Stipendium Hungaricum
scholarships.description: Hungarian government scholarship for students from partner countries to study at Hungarian universities at bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's, doctoral or non-degree level. It includes a stipend and a free Hungarian language course.
scholarships.eligibility: Your country must have an education cooperation agreement with Hungary and you must be nominated by your sending partner. Apply only to programmes covered by that agreement. Entrance exam score of at least 56/100 is needed for final awards. Partner list includes Burundi, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda; South Sudan and Somalia were not listed.
scholarships.award_value: Monthly stipend, housing allowance, free language course; amounts not stated
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2026/2027 call closed on 15 January 2026. The 2027/2028 call has not been published yet; last year's call was announced on 17 November 2025.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Choose up to two programmes at Hungarian institutions, check with your national sending partner for its own deadline and nomination rules, then register and upload documents at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu. Applications are free.

scholarships.title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Campus France, on behalf of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
scholarships.description: French government scholarship programme for high-level international students at master's and joint doctoral level in selected fields. Students cannot apply directly: French higher education institutions select and submit candidates.
scholarships.eligibility: Master's (including engineering) and joint doctoral programmes in science and technology, or humanities and social sciences (law, political science, economics, management, history, French studies). Only French institutions can submit candidates; direct applications are ineligible. The page read does not state nationality or age rules; check the 2027 regulations document.
scholarships.award_value: Master's EUR 1,200/month, PhD EUR 2,100/month; tuition not covered
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2027 call page gives 6 January 2027 in one place and 8 January 2027 in another for institutions to submit; student deadlines are earlier and set by the institution. Not treated as a confirmed date.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Contact Campus France in your country and the international office of a French institution to learn its deadline. The institution must accept and support you and submit your file online.

scholarships.title: Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship
scholarships.description: Undergraduate scholarship for outstanding international students entering the University of Toronto, based on academic achievement, creativity and leadership potential. Roughly 37 scholars are chosen each year.
scholarships.eligibility: International student needing a study permit, in the final year of secondary school in 2026/2027 or graduated no earlier than June 2026, starting first-entry undergraduate study at U of T in September 2027. Must be nominated by their school, which may nominate one student per year. Students already in post-secondary study are ineligible.
scholarships.award_value: Tuition, books, fees and full residence for four years
scholarships.deadline_note: For 2027 entry only students nominated by their school could apply; the school nomination deadline was 9 October 2026. Check the official page for the next intake.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Your school must nominate you through U of T's nomination form. Nominated students then submit the admission application and the scholarship application with documents by the deadlines.

scholarships.title: Mandela Rhodes Scholarship
scholarships.description: Postgraduate scholarship for young African graduates to study an Honours or two-year Master's degree at a recognised South African institution. It includes leadership development.
scholarships.eligibility: Citizen of an African country, aged 19 to 29 in the year of application. Able to study in English. By 1 January 2028, must hold an undergraduate degree with excellent results (above 70% or upper-second class Honours). Funds Honours or Master's study in any field in South Africa, not undergraduate study.
scholarships.award_value: Tuition, accommodation, meals, allowances and travel to South Africa
scholarships.deadline_note: Class of 2027 applications are closed. Class of 2028 applications open on 9 March 2027; an exact closing date is not stated (cycle runs about March to November).
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply online through the application platform on the website. Read the timeline and conditions, attend the compulsory workshop if shortlisted, and prepare documents such as a passport copy and SAQA verification if studying outside South Africa.

scholarships.title: Rhodes Scholarship - East Africa Constituency
scholarships.description: Postgraduate scholarship to study at least two years at the University of Oxford, awarded for academic excellence and character. East Africa has its own constituency with one scholarship per year; Kenya has a separate constituency.
scholarships.eligibility: Citizen of Burundi, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania or Uganda, resident in these or Kenya for five of the last ten years. Aged 18-24 on 1 Oct 2026, or under 27 with a first degree completed on or after 1 July 2025. Undergraduate degree completed by July 2027 and Oxford entry requirements met. Kenyans apply via the Kenya constituency. Ethiopia, Somalia and DR Congo are not in this constituency.
scholarships.award_value: Covers at least 2 years at Oxford; amounts not stated on page
scholarships.deadline_note: The 2027 cohort window ran 1 June to 27 August 2026 and is closed. Dates for the next cycle are not published yet.
scholarships.how_to_apply: Apply online only, with no fee, during the window using the button on the East Africa page. You need a CV, four to five referees, academic and personal statements, and ID. Finalists are interviewed and must then be admitted to Oxford.
